headline: High: LightAgent’s broad egress and MCP/browser tooling can leak or mis-handle PDF content when paired with pdf.js, while shared document workflows create injection and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP and browsers, so it may ingest content from pdf.js-rendered documents or shared files as instructions. pdf.js processes PDFs and can surface attacker-controlled document text. The pair has a plausible shared-document bridge, but no direct evidence of automatic instruction parsing, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF LightAgent reads pdf.js output or shared PDFs as trusted instructions
IF a PDF contains instruction-like text that is forwarded into MCP or browser workflows
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on PDF-derived text
Route pdf.js output through a human review step
Use separate workspaces for raw PDFs and agent prompts
Add provenance labels to all PDF-derived content
requires-engineering: enforce content-type filtering before MCP/tool calls

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and has broad network egress, so sensitive PDF content can leave the local boundary. pdf.js handles PDF files locally, but when paired with LightAgent the combined workflow can expose document contents to external APIs by default. The blast radius includes secrets and workflow state, so high fits.
conditions: IF PDF content is passed from pdf.js into LightAgent prompts or tool results
IF LightAgent sends those prompts or results to external inference APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive PDFs out of LightAgent workflows
Disable network egress for the LightAgent runtime
Use a local-only inference backend
Separate storage for PDFs and agent memory
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any outbound call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and LightAgent can spawn subprocesses while pdf.js runs in a browser-based worker model. If they share a writable workspace or the same PDF artifacts, concurrent edits or overwrites can occur. The profiles do not prove shared write access, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same PDF workspace or output directory
IF concurrent runs modify the same artifact without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Run only one writer per PDF artifact
Add file-locking around shared outputs
Use read-only mounts for pdf.js inputs
requires-engineering: implement optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can generate tool results and workflow state that pdf.js may consume indirectly in a document-processing pipeline. If pdf.js renders or acts on LightAgent output without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect document handling. There is no direct evidence of autonomous downstream action, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF pdf.js consumes LightAgent-produced text or metadata as authoritative
IF no verification step checks LightAgent output before rendering or acting on it
mitigations: Insert a validation step before pdf.js consumes agent output
Require human approval for generated document metadata
Compare outputs against source PDFs before use
Log and diff all transformed fields
requires-engineering: add schema validation for inter-agent handoff

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent explicitly handles api_key and tot_api_key secrets and broad user data, while pdf.js is a document processor with no stated retention or residency controls. The pair can therefore create retention or handling mismatches for sensitive documents and secrets. Because only LightAgent shows sensitive-data handling, the other agent is not separately cited beyond its document-processing role.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed through LightAgent and pdf.js together
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the same PDF data class
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated PDFs through the pair
Minimize secret-bearing fields in prompts
Set explicit retention limits for logs and outputs
Store PDFs in a compliant region
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling policy
